Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`16e014b9-1631-4a69-92d1-dbf92ad6b5ae`](16e014b9-1631-4a69-92d1-dbf92ad6b5ae).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

Applies: PRIN-003, PRIN-005, PRIN-008

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `8040e219394c8f03ed9be57ef4dce33a1948c694` of `main`. The dispatcher refuses to clone (so this PR would not exist) unless both hold at dispatch time: the worker checkout's own revision is a confirmed, current ancestor of local `main` (`worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`), and `main` itself is a confirmed ancestor-or-equal of its own tracking upstream -- carries no commit absent from it (`dispatch.ensure_base_ref_current`; `BaseRefStatus.wrong`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

This attempt resumed from preserved work: the latest of https://github.com/grantbest/homelabv2/pull/1059 was applied as the clone's starting point before the worker's first action (OPS-106). The revision above is the base the baseline was applied onto, not the tree verification ran against -- that tree is base + baseline + this attempt's work.

## Intent

Closes two present-day routes by which code a worker controls runs as the dispatcher's own user (grantbest, uid 501), outside every sandbox. The factory worker runs as that same user today, and part B (a separate uid) is still in design. MEASURED 2026-09-26 at origin/main d4b6d80c. Anchors drift, so locate by symbol. ROUTE 1, dev.finding bd4b2a9a. dispatch.materialize_personas (dispatch.py:2128-2136) runs `[sys.executable, <clone>/scripts/materialize_agents.py, <clone>]` with subprocess.run, unsandboxed. It is reached through dispatch.prepare_worker_argv (:2139-2150, the call at :2148), which activities/dispatch_steps.py calls at :303 inside _run_worker_with_heartbeat. That happens AFTER run_activity has applied apply_preserved_baseline (activities/dispatch_steps.py:888). A preserved attempt is a prior worker's UNGATED diff, so a failed attempt can plant a scripts/materialize_agents.py that the next attempt's dispatcher executes as grantbest. WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES (scripts/materialize_agents.py, 58 lines): it copies the two files named in PERSONAS = ('polecat-developer.md', 'architect-sme.md') from docs/agents/ under ITS OWN repo root (REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]) into <destination>/.claude/agents/. Because the clone's copy is run, REPO_ROOT is the clone, so the persona SOURCES come from the clone. That is what the docstring's 'so the tested tree defines the personas' means: the tested tree supplies the persona DATA. Nothing requires the tested tree's CODE to do the copying. DESIGN CHOICE: the simplest correct option is to run no clone code at all. The dispatcher copies <clone>/docs/agents/<name> to <clone>/.claude/agents/<name> in-process, for the names it already declares (dispatch.POLECAT_PERSONA and dispatch.ARCHITECT_PERSONA, dispatch.py:2041-2042, the same pair assemble_personas_prompt already reads through _persona_body :2091-2103). That keeps the data from the tested tree and the logic in merged code. The two alternatives were rejected. (a) Running the MERGED copy of the script as a subprocess against the clone would still start a process as grantbest, and it cannot take the clone as its data source without editing the script, because REPO_ROOT is derived from __file__. (b) Running the clone's copy inside the worker containment profile still executes planted code, and costs more lines. Neither beats a two-file copy. The copy must not become a new escape of its own: a preserved diff can create symlinks (git mode 120000). So a persona SOURCE that is a symlink, or that resolves outside the clone, would make the dispatcher read an arbitrary file into the clone (for example ~/.factory-dispatcher/env, which the worker profile denies reading). A symlinked DESTINATION (.claude, .claude/agents, or an existing persona file) would make it write outside the clone. The same source rule therefore also covers _persona_body, which reads the same files into the worker's system prompt. ROUTE 2, dev.finding 32f631c1. dispatch.smoke_check_python (dispatch.py:2696-2706; argv at :2701-2703) byte-compiles changed files with cwd=clone. The smoke check SHALL run the interpreter in isolated mode (-I), so no module from the clone's working directory, in source or compiled form, is ever imported (dev.finding 32f631c1). The finding records the case in detail; this spec cites it by id. -I is line-neutral. It also ignores PYTHON* environment variables and the user site-packages directory. py_compile needs neither, and the launchd env file sets no PYTHON* name (checked by name). SIZE. `cat apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py apps/factory-dispatcher/guards.py | wc -l` = 8,555 at d4b6d80c (7,172 + 1,383). The arc rule is strictly below 8,556 at every merge, so dispatch.py must be net 0 or negative. New logic goes in containment.py. materialize_personas's body shrinks from a subprocess call to a helper call (about -5), _persona_body swaps two lines for two, and smoke_check_python's `-I` is inside an existing line. COMPOSITION, checked 2026-09-26 against open PRs and the filed or merged specs. PR 1049 (11f7792a, the codex WorkerEntry deletion) edits containment.py's docstring and dispatch.py's registry: disjoint hunks, rebase. 4ae17659 (OPS-122) adds the worker-environment builder to containment.py and edits run_worker's env lines. 940e596f (SEC-6c19f60f) adds the verification profile to containment.py and edits dispatch.py :3039-3232. 8fe64a23 (SEC-019909c0 + 75b50b58 + dd648709) adds the deny helper to containment.py. All of these are disjoint hunks from this bead's (new containment.py functions; dispatch.py :2091-2136 and :2701-2703), so whichever merges second rebases and re-verifies. 9c65dd68 (SEC-a0166920-2, the child-environment migration) lists materialize_personas (dispatch.py:2132) as a spawn site to route through child_env. After this bead that site no longer spawns anything. The migration's AC-5 meta-assertion re-derives its site list from the ast, and the seam's ratchet constant (4dc883a3) only has to be at most the count, so a drop of one breaks neither. smoke_check_python goes through dispatch.run, whose environment the migration narrows: that is compatible. Part B (design-partB-r3, in design) runs materialization as the worker uid in split mode and never calls dispatch.materialize_personas there. This bead is the uid-501 path and does not conflict. The outer loop's claim-cfg fix (claim_activity, activities/dispatch_steps.py:466-473) does not overlap. D7: every acceptance criterion is measured against fixture clones under tmp_path. Nothing reads the live store, the live env file or any live process.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: smoke_check_python RUNS ISOLATED. Its argv SHALL become `[sys.executable, '-I', '-m', 'py_compile', *py_files]`, with cwd, the file filter and the return contract unchanged. Linux-runnable tests, each with a fixture clone under tmp_path and a module named py_compile in the clone's working directory whose import would be observable (it writes a marker outside the clone): (a) THE MODULE AS SOURCE. smoke_check_python(clone, ['ok.py']) returns None, and the module is not imported. (b) THE MODULE IN COMPILED FORM ONLY, built by the test for sys.executable, with no source beside it. smoke_check_python(clone, ['ok.py']) returns None, and the module is not imported. (c) CONTROLS, one for each of (a) and (b), which make them non-vacuous. The old invocation, `[sys.executable, '-m', 'py_compile', 'ok.py']` with cwd=clone, DOES import the module, so neither test can pass on an interpreter whose import rules change. (d) A file with a syntax error still returns a non-empty error string. The existing tests/test_base_verification_check_wiring.py:614 use SHALL pass unmodified.
- AC-2: PERSONAS ARE MATERIALIZED IN-PROCESS FROM THE CLONE'S DATA, AND NO CLONE CODE RUNS. containment.py SHALL gain two functions. (i) persona_source(clone, name) returns the path of <clone>/docs/agents/<name> only when that path is not a symlink (os.lstat), is a regular file, and resolves to a path inside clone.resolve(); otherwise it returns None. (ii) materialize_personas(clone, names) copies each source's bytes to <clone>/.claude/agents/<name>, and returns None on success or a reason string. <clone>/.claude and <clone>/.claude/agents SHALL be created when absent, without following links, as the old script's mkdir did. Every OSError raised while creating those directories, unlinking, opening, reading or writing SHALL be caught and turned into a refusal. It SHALL refuse, with a reason that names only the clone-relative path (for example `.claude/agents/polecat-developer.md`) and a stable class (for example 'not a regular file', 'symlink refused', 'outside the clone', 'could not be written'), when: a source fails (i); <clone>/.claude or <clone>/.claude/agents exists as a symlink or resolves outside the clone; or a destination cannot be written without following a link. An existing destination entry (a file or a symlink) is unlinked first, and the file is written with os.open(O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW), so no write lands outside the clone. dispatch.materialize_personas(clone) SHALL call it with (POLECAT_PERSONA, ARCHITECT_PERSONA) and SHALL raise on a reason. Every refusal raises DispatchEnvironmentError, the type today's missing-persona path already raises. The refusal happens in prepare_worker_argv, before any worker result exists. activities/dispatch_steps.py's record step sends every such pre-worker exception to record_environment_failure (the `if "worker_result" not in state` branch), whatever its type, so choosing DispatchError would not charge an attempt either, and would only make the name lie. The consequence is stated in the PR body: a preserved baseline that plants a refused persona path is recorded as an environmental fault with no attempt charged, and the per-bead breaker (trailing_environmental_fault_streak, bound 3) latches that bead. The outer loop then fences it or requeues it without its preserved attempts. The reason text SHALL be stable across dispatches: no timestamps, counts, absolute paths or errno strings that carry a path. The clone is a new random temporary directory on every run, so any absolute path would make a new fault signature each time, and the breaker would never latch. It SHALL start no subprocess and SHALL neither read nor execute <clone>/scripts/materialize_agents.py. dispatch._persona_body SHALL obtain its path through containment.persona_source with the same classification, so no refused file's content reaches the prompt. scripts/materialize_agents.py SHALL NOT change: operators and part B's launcher still use it.
- AC-3: THE TESTS FOR AC-2. These are Linux-runnable, with fixture clones under tmp_path, each clone carrying docs/agents/polecat-developer.md and docs/agents/architect-sme.md with front matter. (a) PLANTED MATERIALIZER. <clone>/scripts/materialize_agents.py, when run, writes a marker outside the clone and writes a bogus .claude/agents/polecat-developer.md. After dispatch.materialize_personas(clone), the marker SHALL NOT exist, and each .claude/agents/<name> SHALL be byte-identical to the clone's docs/agents/<name>. (b) THE TESTED TREE DEFINES THE PERSONAS. Edit the clone's docs/agents/polecat-developer.md, and the materialized copy carries the edit. (c) NO SUBPROCESS. With subprocess.run and subprocess.Popen monkeypatched to fail the test if called, (a) still passes. (d) SYMLINKED SOURCE. docs/agents/architect-sme.md is a symlink to <tmp>/outside/secret.txt, which holds a fixture marker string. dispatch.materialize_personas raises DispatchEnvironmentError naming docs/agents/architect-sme.md. dispatch.assemble_personas_prompt(clone, {'risk_class': 'behavioral'}) raises the same way. The marker string appears in no file under <clone>/.claude and in neither exception's message. (e) SYMLINKED DESTINATION DIRECTORY. <clone>/.claude/agents is a symlink to <tmp>/outside-dir: DispatchEnvironmentError, and <tmp>/outside-dir stays empty. (e2) <clone>/.claude/agents/polecat-developer.md is a DIRECTORY, and (e3) <clone>/.claude/agents is a REGULAR FILE: each raises DispatchEnvironmentError. (e4) With <clone>/.claude absent, materialization succeeds and creates it. For EVERY refusal case, (d), (e), (e2) and (e3): the reason is an identical string across two calls on two differently-named tmp clones, and contains no absolute path (neither clone's path nor tmp_path appears in it). (f) SYMLINKED DESTINATION FILE. An existing .claude/agents/polecat-developer.md that is a symlink to <tmp>/outside-file: after materialization the outside file is byte-unchanged, and the destination is a regular file carrying the clone's persona. (g) A MISSING SOURCE raises DispatchEnvironmentError, as today. (h) DRIFT GUARD. {dispatch.POLECAT_PERSONA, dispatch.ARCHITECT_PERSONA} equals set(PERSONAS) of the scripts/materialize_agents.py in the dispatcher's own repository, loaded by file path from Path(dispatch.__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'scripts' / 'materialize_agents.py'. The existing tests/test_claude_worker.py assemble_personas_prompt tests and scripts/tests/test_materialize_agents.py SHALL pass unmodified.
- AC-4: SIZE AND PLACEMENT. dispatch.py's net line change against the PR's merge-base SHALL be at most 0; guards.py and scripts/** SHALL be unchanged. The PR body SHALL quote `cat apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py apps/factory-dispatcher/guards.py | wc -l` at the merge-base and at the head, and containment.py's line count before and after. containment.py's module docstring SHALL gain one short paragraph saying three things: the dispatcher materializes personas in-process from the clone's docs/agents because running the clone's materializer ran worker-controlled code as the dispatcher's user (bd4b2a9a); persona files are read only when they are regular files inside the clone and not symlinks; and the destination is written without following links.
- AC-5: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, STATED IN THE PR BODY IN THESE TERMS. Other places where clone-derived code runs as the dispatcher's user remain, and each is owned elsewhere. (1) Declared verification and its bootstrap pip install run unsandboxed until SEC-6c19f60f (940e596f) merges. (2) The worker can write <clone>/.git under the current profile, and the dispatcher's later unsandboxed git operations in that clone, at least the propose and preserved-baseline commits, can be affected by what it writes there. This route is OPEN and is NOT owned by this bead; it is dev.finding 79db3113, closed by its own spec. (3) The base-revision check runs main's code in a worktree, not worker code. (4) The worker itself runs as the same uid until part B. (5) py_compile still writes __pycache__ files into the clone. The worker states in the PR body that it did not probe any live process.
- AC-6: Stage every new or changed file (`git add`, not commit) before the final verification run (dev.finding 94d7258f). The PR body SHALL quote the collected test counts for apps/factory-dispatcher/tests before and after, SHALL declare exactly one `Change kind: behavioral`, and SHALL name any test that SKIPPED inside the worker's own sandbox and why.

## Declared scope

Allowed: apps/factory-dispatcher/containment.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/
Forbidden: .github/**, .github/workflows/**, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, docs/**, infrastructure/**, scripts/**, apps/substrate/**, apps/mcp-hub/**, apps/lifeops-console/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/guards.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/config.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/substrate.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/worker.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/launchd_agent.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/file_task.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/activities/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/workflows/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/tasks/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/conftest.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/fixtures/**

Dispatcher scope verdict: **all changes within scope**

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

## Worker's own report

```
Both required test additions are done, verified against the code (including a manual mutation check confirming they fail without the guard they protect), and everything is staged. Here's the summary:

## Changes
Added to `apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/test_persona_materialization.py` only (no production code touched — `dispatch.py` and `containment.py` are untouched by this attempt):

1. **`docs/agents` / `docs` symlinked outside the clone** (`test_docs_or_docs_agents_symlinked_outside_clone_refused`, 2 parametrized cases): asserts `dispatch.materialize_personas` and `dispatch.assemble_personas_prompt` both raise `DispatchEnvironmentError` naming `docs/agents/polecat-developer.md: outside the clone`, and that no outside marker content reaches `.claude`. Both new fault functions (`_fault_docs_agents_symlinked_outside`, `_fault_docs_symlinked_outside`) are also added to the two-clone reason-stability parametrization.
2. **(e3) `.claude/agents` as a regular file** (`test_claude_agents_is_regular_file_refused`), plus `_fault_claude_agents_is_regular_file` added to the stability parametrization.

**Verified these are load-bearing**, not decorative: I temporarily deleted the `if not _resolve_inside(clone_root, path): return "outside the clone"` line from `containment.py` and reran — both new outside-clone tests failed with `DID NOT RAISE`, confirming they close the gap the release gate flagged. Restored the line before running the full suite (confirmed via `git diff --stat` showing zero change to `containment.py`).

## Verification run
- `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/ -q`: **2308 passed, 11 failed, 7 skipped**. The 11 failures are all in `test_dispatch.py` and pre-exist this change — they compare against `dispatch.DEFAULT_OPERATOR` and fail because this sandbox's env resolves it to `outer-loop/claude` instead of `operator`; unrelated to any file this bead touches. The 7 skips are `test_containment.py`(×2)/`test_gate_containment.py`(×5) sandbox-exec/nested-sandbox unavailability inside this worker's own sandbox.
- `python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_materialize_agents.py scripts/tests/test_personas_invariant.py -q`: **7 passed**.
- `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`: **all repository invariants passed**.
- `ruff check` on `containment.py`, `dispatch.py`, and the changed test file: all checks passed.
- The worker did not probe any live process (AC-5): all execution was against fixture clones under `tmp_path`; the only non-test reads were `git cat-file`/`wc -l` against local git history for line counts.

## Counts
- `apps/factory-dispatcher/tests` collected: **2320 → 2326** (+6).
- `test_persona_materialization.py`: **15 → 21** tests. `test_smoke_check_isolation.py`: unchanged at **5**.
- `dispatch.py` + `guards.py`: merge-base (50fb6194) **8555** (7172+1383) → head **8552** (7169+1383) — `dispatch.py` net **-3**, `guards.py` unchanged, both untouched this attempt.
- `containment.py`: **179 → 321** lines (+142, from the prior attempt; unchanged this attempt).

Change kind: behavioral

I did not write `.factory/design.md` — this bead's hard scope boundary for this run lists only `containment.py`, `dispatch.py`, and `tests/` as writable, and the required work (closing two review-flagged test gaps) needed no new design decision beyond what the merged implementation already encodes.

Everything is staged (`git add`) and ready for the dispatcher's own verification pass.
```
